title: Chemical Bond Rotation Angle Measurement
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive 3D chemical bond rotation angle (dihedral angle) measurement tool.

SCENE SETUP:
- Black background, perspective camera at position (0, 3, 8) looking at origin.
- Ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 10, 7) with intensity 0.8.
- Render a chain of exactly 4 atoms (A, B, C, D) connected by 3 bonds in a zigzag arrangement.
  - Atom A: red sphere (radius 0.4) at (-3, 0, 0)
  - Atom B: blue sphere (radius 0.4) at (-1, 1, 0)
  - Atom C: green sphere (radius 0.4) at (1, -0.5, 0)
  - Atom D: yellow sphere (radius 0.4) at (3, 0.5, 0)
- Bonds are white cylinders (radius 0.08) connecting adjacent atoms.
- OrbitControls for camera rotation (damping enabled).

DIHEDRAL ANGLE MEASUREMENT:
- The dihedral angle is defined by the four atoms A-B-C-D. It measures the angle between the plane formed by A-B-C and the plane formed by B-C-D.
- Compute the dihedral angle using the standard method: vectors BA, BC, CD; normals n1 = BA×BC, n2 = BC×CD; angle = atan2((n1×n2)·normalize(BC), n1·n2). Display in degrees [-180, 180].
- Draw a translucent arc (torus segment or line curve) between the two planes near the B-C bond midpoint to visualize the dihedral angle. Color it orange.

INTERACTION - ATOM DRAGGING:
- Users can click and drag Atom A or Atom D in 3D space (constrained to a plane parallel to the camera). Use raycasting to detect clicks on atoms.
- While dragging, the atom position updates in real time, bonds re-draw, and the dihedral angle recalculates live.
- Atoms B and C are fixed and cannot be dragged.

INTERACTION - PRESET CONFORMATIONS:
- Add 4 HTML buttons at the top-left of the screen:
  - 'Eclipsed (0°)': snaps atom D so dihedral = 0°
  - 'Gauche (60°)': snaps atom D so dihedral = 60°
  - 'Anti (180°)': snaps atom D so dihedral = 180°
  - 'Custom (-90°)': snaps atom D so dihedral = -90°
- When a preset is clicked, animate atom D smoothly (over 500ms) to the target position using a rotation around the B-C axis. Keep atom D at the same distance from C as its initial distance.

INTERACTION - KEYBOARD:
- Press 'R' to reset all atoms to their original positions.
- Press '+' or '=' to increase the dihedral angle by 5 degrees (rotate atom D around B-C axis).
- Press '-' to decrease the dihedral angle by 5 degrees.
- Press 'M' to toggle measurement visibility (the arc and angle label).

HUD / UI:
- Display a HUD overlay (HTML div, top-right corner, white text on semi-transparent dark background, 220px wide) showing:
  - 'Dihedral Angle: XX.X°'
  - 'Atom A: (x, y, z)' (1 decimal place)
  - 'Atom D: (x, y, z)' (1 decimal place)
  - 'Conformation: <name>' where name is 'Eclipsed', 'Gauche+', 'Gauche-', 'Anti', 'Staggered', or 'Custom' based on angle ranges.
- Conformation classification: Eclipsed = |angle| < 10°, Gauche+ = 50° < angle < 70°, Gauche- = -70° < angle < -50°, Anti = |angle| > 170°, otherwise 'Custom'.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
  - atomPositions: array of 4 objects [{x,y,z}, ...] for atoms A,B,C,D
  - dihedralAngle: number in degrees [-180, 180]
  - conformationName: string
  - measurementVisible: boolean (true initially)
  - selectedAtom: null or index (0 for A, 3 for D) of currently dragged atom
  - isDragging: boolean
  - animating: boolean (true during preset animation)
  - bondLengths: array of 3 numbers [AB, BC, CD] distances
  - presetHistory: array of strings recording which preset buttons were clicked (push name on each click)
  - angleStepCount: number tracking net +/- key presses (starts at 0, +1 for increase, -1 for decrease)
physics_constraints: Dihedral angle must be computed correctly using the cross-product method and remain in [-180, 180] range. Bond lengths BC must remain constant (atoms B and C are fixed). When rotating atom D via presets or keyboard, it must rotate around the B-C axis maintaining constant distance from atom C. All atom positions must be finite (no NaN/Infinity). Conformation classification must match the defined angle ranges.
